form.label: SSH — Network Devices
form.description: Pull show version / license / NTP / certificate data from Cisco devices over SSH.

html.p: Some data lives only on a device's CLI. Here Splunk logs into the Cisco router over SSH every 5 minutes (scripted input ssh_router.sh), runs a set of show commands, and indexes the output — no agent on the device. London → london_network, Berlin → berlin_network (so Leo/Ben see their own site, Gary sees both).
Pick a site above. Each panel shows the latest captured output for that command.

search.query: (index=london_network OR index=berlin_network) sourcetype=cisco:ios site=$site$ | stats latest(_time) as last | eval last=strftime(last,"%F %T")

(index=london_network OR index=berlin_network) sourcetype=cisco:ios site=$site$ | stats latest(_time) as last by command host | eval "Last seen"=strftime(last,"%F %T") | rename command as Command, host as Device | table Command Device "Last seen" | sort Command
(index=london_network OR index=berlin_network) sourcetype=cisco:ios site=$site$ command="show version" | sort -_time | head 1
(index=london_network OR index=berlin_network) sourcetype=cisco:ios site=$site$ command="show license summary" | sort -_time | head 1
(index=london_network OR index=berlin_network) sourcetype=cisco:ios site=$site$ command="show ntp status" | sort -_time | head 1
(index=london_network OR index=berlin_network) sourcetype=cisco:ios site=$site$ command="show crypto pki certificates" | sort -_time | head 1

html.p: Devices are listed in bin/routers.csv (site, host, user, password). inputs.conf runs one scripted input per site:
html.pre: [script://./bin/ssh_router.sh london] index = london_network sourcetype = cisco:ios interval = 300
html.p: Needs sshpass on the Splunk host (apply.sh installs it). If a panel is empty, check the "Commands captured" table — a command that errors (e.g. not supported / no privilege) still indexes its error text so you can see what happened. SSH legacy algorithms are enabled in the script in case the IOS device only offers older KEX/ciphers.
